headline: Phillies fall to Brewers 4-1 as two homers doom Nola
recap: The Phillies lost to the Milwaukee Brewers 4-1 at Citizens Bank Park on Wednesday night. Brice Turang homered in the top of the first to put Milwaukee ahead 1-0, and Christian Yelich homered in the top of the second to make it 2-0. Philadelphia answered in the bottom of the second, cutting the deficit to 2-1 when J.T. Realmuto grounded out to second base with Alec Bohm scoring from third. Milwaukee pulled away in the top of the third when William Contreras singled home Garrett Mitchell and Turang, making it 4-1, and neither team scored again. Aaron Nola (7-11) took the loss, allowing four runs, including both home runs, on four hits over six innings with eight strikeouts and one walk. Bryson Stott had two doubles for the Phillies, who stranded 10 runners and were held to six hits by Brewers starter Logan Henderson (11-3) and three relievers, capped by Trevor Megill's 30th save.
The loss dropped Philadelphia to 87-71, second in the NL East, six games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves (93-65), and extended the Phillies' losing streak to one game.

Philadelphia hosts Milwaukee again Thursday at Citizens Bank Park in the finale of their three-game series, with Andrew Painter starting for the Phillies against Brewers right-hander Bryse Wilson. First pitch is scheduled for 6:05 PM ET. Philadelphia is favored at -120 on the moneyline, with Milwaukee at +100.
